artworks.title: Iphis and Ianthe
artworks.description: Metamorphoses plate — Iphis and Ianthe at the Cretan wedding Isis will make possible.

artworks.title: Iphis Transformed into a Young Man
artworks.description: Dutch engraving of Ovid IX — the body remade on the eve of the rites so Iphis may marry Ianthe.

artworks.title: Telethusa and Iphis Pray to Isis
artworks.description: Mother and child before Isis — Ligdus' vow answered by the Egyptian goddess who walks Ovid's Crete.

artworks.title: Isis and Iphis
artworks.description: Baur's Ovid plate — Isis granting the transformation that lets the Cretan wedding proceed.

popCulture.title: Iphis
popCulture.description: Ovid's Cretan wedding tale — a girl raised as a boy, love for Ianthe, and Isis' gift of a male body on the eve of the rites.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book IX holds Ligdus' vow, Telethusa's deception, and the goddess who answers a mother's prayer — still the West's classic sex-change myth.

popCulture.title: Isis
popCulture.description: The Egyptian goddess who walks Ovid's Crete — the deity Telethusa trusts when no Greek god will remake her child.
